pinyin: zhì zhī sǐ dì ér hòu shēng
literal: put · them · death · ground · then · live
natural: fight with your back to the wall

meaning.en: Only when put in a desperate situation will people fight to survive.
meaning.zh: 把人置于绝境，他们才会拼死求生，反而获得生路。

equivalents: fight with one's back to the wall

examples.zh: 公司濒临破产，他决定置之死地而后生，转型做电商。
examples.en: With the firm near bankruptcy, he decided to stake everything and move into e-commerce.

examples.zh: 背水一战，置之死地而后生。
examples.en: Fight with your back to the river; from the brink of death comes life.

examples.zh: 有时只有置之死地而后生，才能激发潜力。
examples.en: Sometimes only a desperate situation unlocks one's potential.

story.en: Han Xin led his troops across the river and fought with the water behind them at Jingxing, winning against great odds; he explained it as 'put them in a fatal position and they live'.
story.zh: 韩信井陉之战背水列阵，大破赵军，后解释说：“兵法不曰：陷之死地而后生，置之亡地而后存？”

usage.en: Often used as a strategy or motto; formal.

meaning.en: A plan with no risk of failure.
meaning.zh: 非常周全、不会出差错的办法。

examples.zh: 目前还没有万全之策，只能走一步看一步。
examples.en: There's no foolproof plan yet; we'll take it one step at a time.

examples.zh: 为求万全之策，我们请专家论证了三次。
examples.en: To be safe, we had experts review it three times.

examples.zh: 世上没有万全之策，总得冒点险。
examples.en: There is no risk-free plan; you must take some risk.

usage.en: Often in negation: 没有万全之策.
usage.zh: 常用否定：没有万全之策。

meaning.en: To get up early and go to bed late; to work tirelessly.
meaning.zh: 早起晚睡，形容勤奋不懈。

equivalents: burn the candle at both ends

examples.zh: 他夙兴夜寐，只为完成这个研究。
examples.en: He rose early and slept late for the sake of this research.

examples.zh: 创业初期，大家夙兴夜寐，毫无怨言。
examples.en: In the early days of the startup, everyone worked long hours without complaint.

examples.zh: 夙兴夜寐的父母，供孩子读完了大学。
examples.en: The hard-working parents saw their child through university.

story.en: Book of Songs, 'The Simple Fellow': a wife recalls rising early and sleeping late through the years of her marriage (夙兴夜寐，靡有朝矣).

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

meaning.en: Obstinate and resistant to change or persuasion.
meaning.zh: 十分固执，不肯改变旧观念、旧习惯。

examples.zh: 他顽固不化，谁劝都不听。
examples.en: He is hopelessly stubborn and won't listen to anyone.

examples.zh: 面对新事物，一些人仍然顽固不化。
examples.en: Some are still set in their ways when faced with new things.

examples.zh: 这种顽固不化的态度只会让问题恶化。
examples.en: Such an obstinate attitude will only make things worse.

synonyms: 茅坑里的石头——又臭又硬

meaning.en: Being disunited, with people no longer sharing one mind or goal.
meaning.zh: 指不同心，意见不一致，彼此不再团结。

examples.zh: 领导层离心离德，公司很快垮了。
examples.en: With the leadership divided in purpose, the company soon collapsed.

examples.zh: 团队离心离德，很难取得好成绩。
examples.en: A team lacking unity can hardly achieve good results.

examples.zh: 内部离心离德是失败的根源。
examples.en: Internal disunity is the root of defeat.

story.en: Book of Documents: King Wu says of the Shang tyrant Zhou that he has 'a hundred thousand ministers but a hundred thousand minds' while he himself has 'ten ministers, one mind and one virtue' (同心同德).
story.zh: 《尚书》：“受有臣億万，惟億万心；予有臣三千，惟一心。”

date.zh: 东晋 · 约4世纪初（伪古文《尚书》篇章）
date.en: Eastern Jin, early 4th c. (spurious “Old Text” chapter of the Book of Documents)

meaning.en: Impressively imposing from every angle.
meaning.zh: 形容气势很盛，神气十足，使人敬畏。

examples.zh: 将军骑在马上，威风八面。
examples.en: The general on horseback looked commanding.

examples.zh: 他穿上制服，顿时威风八面。
examples.en: In uniform he suddenly looked imposing.

examples.zh: 舞狮队威风八面地走进场。
examples.en: The lion-dance troupe strode in with great swagger.

usage.en: Predicate; also written 八面威风.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，也说“八面威风”。

meaning.en: To abuse power and lord it over others.
meaning.zh: 擅自使用权势，欺压别人。

examples.zh: 他当上经理后就在下属面前作威作福。
examples.en: Once made manager, he threw his weight around in front of his staff.

examples.zh: 官员不能在群众面前作威作福。
examples.en: Officials must not lord it over the public.

examples.zh: 别以为有点权力就能作威作福。
examples.en: Don't think a little power lets you bully others.

story.en: Book of Documents: 'Only the ruler may bestow blessings, wield authority and enjoy delicacies' (惟辟作福，惟辟作威); later used for officials who abuse power.
story.zh: 《尚书·洪范》：“惟辟作福，惟辟作威，惟辟玉食。臣无有作福作威玉食。”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前11—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 11th–3rd c. BC

meaning.en: A heroic woman.
meaning.zh: 指有英雄气概的女子。

examples.zh: 花木兰是家喻户晓的巾帼英雄。
examples.en: Hua Mulan is a household-name heroine.

examples.zh: 她被评为抗疫中的巾帼英雄。
examples.en: She was named a heroine of the fight against the epidemic.

examples.zh: 女运动员们个个是巾帼英雄。
examples.en: Every one of the women athletes is a heroine.

meaning.en: To replace one form of violence or tyranny with another.
meaning.zh: 用暴力代替暴力，指用残暴的手段推翻暴政后，自己又行暴政。

examples.zh: 武力报复只会以暴易暴，冤冤相报。
examples.en: Retaliating by force only means violence begets violence.

examples.zh: 他们推翻暴君后，却又以暴易暴。
examples.en: After toppling the tyrant, they became tyrants themselves.

examples.zh: 解决纠纷不能以暴易暴。
examples.en: Disputes must not be settled by answering violence with violence.

story.en: Boyi and Shuqi, protesting King Wu's attack on the Shang, sang: 'He has replaced violence with violence and does not know his wrong' (以暴易暴兮，不知其非矣).
story.zh: 伯夷、叔齐采薇而歌：“以暴易暴兮，不知其非矣。”

meaning.en: To talk rambling and aimlessly with no clear point.
meaning.zh: 说话漫无边际，没有中心。

examples.zh: 别东拉西扯了，说正事吧。
examples.en: Stop rambling and get to the point.

examples.zh: 他东拉西扯半天，也没说到重点。
examples.en: He rambled for ages without reaching the point.

examples.zh: 她们东拉西扯，聊了一下午。
examples.en: They chatted away about this and that all afternoon.

meaning.en: To go to war, or act, without a just cause.
meaning.zh: 出兵没有正当理由，比喻做事没有正当名义。

examples.zh: 这次出兵师出无名，遭到国际谴责。
examples.en: The troop deployment lacked just cause and drew international condemnation.

examples.zh: 没有证据就抓人，岂不是师出无名？
examples.en: Arresting someone without evidence is acting without grounds.

examples.zh: 他们的指责师出无名，站不住脚。
examples.en: Their accusation has no justification and doesn't hold up.

meaning.en: To help others fulfil their good wishes.
meaning.zh: 帮助别人实现好事或心愿。

examples.zh: 他愿意成人之美，把名额让给了别人。
examples.en: Glad to help another, he gave his place to someone else.

examples.zh: 君子成人之美，不成人之恶。
examples.en: A gentleman helps others to do good, not to do evil.

examples.zh: 请你成人之美，让他们见一面吧。
examples.en: Please do them a kindness and let them meet.

story.en: Confucius: 'The gentleman helps others achieve what is good and does not help them achieve what is bad' (君子成人之美，不成人之恶).
story.zh: 《论语》：“君子成人之美，不成人之恶。小人反是。”

meaning.en: One mistake costing the whole game.
meaning.zh: 一着棋下错，导致全盘失败。

examples.zh: 一步走错，满盘皆输。
examples.en: One wrong step and the whole game is lost.

examples.zh: 投资要谨慎，否则可能满盘皆输。
examples.en: Invest carefully, or you could lose everything.

examples.zh: 他重仓一只股票，结果满盘皆输。
examples.en: He went all in on one stock and lost the lot.

usage.en: Usually 一着不慎，满盘皆输.
usage.zh: 常说“一着不慎，满盘皆输”。

meaning.en: To fight for every inch of ground; refusing to yield.
meaning.zh: 一寸土地也一定要争夺，形容毫不让步。

examples.zh: 守军在阵地上寸土必争。
examples.en: The garrison contested every inch of ground.

examples.zh: 两家公司在市场上寸土必争。
examples.en: The two companies fight for every inch of the market.

examples.zh: 在原则问题上，我们必须寸土必争。
examples.en: On matters of principle we must not give an inch.

usage.en: Predicate; often paired with 寸土不让.

meaning.en: To echo others' opinions without thinking.
meaning.zh: 自己没有主见，别人说什么就跟着说什么。

examples.zh: 开会时他总是随声附和，从不表达自己的看法。
examples.en: At meetings he just echoes others and never gives his own view.

examples.zh: 不要随声附和，要独立思考。
examples.en: Don't just echo; think for yourself.

examples.zh: 网友们随声附和，真相被淹没了。
examples.en: Netizens chimed in blindly and the truth was drowned out.

meaning.en: Looks so lovely that it is like food for the eyes; of beautiful women or scenery.
meaning.zh: 美丽的姿容或景色让人看着就觉得满足。

examples.zh: 山间秀色可餐，令人流连忘返。
examples.en: The mountain scenery is a feast for the eyes and hard to leave.

examples.zh: 她的容貌秀色可餐。
examples.en: Her looks are a feast for the eyes.

examples.zh: 春天的田野秀色可餐。
examples.en: The spring fields are a delight to the eye.

story.en: Lu Ji's poem on a beautiful woman: 'Her fair skin is so lustrous, her loveliness seems good enough to eat' (鲜肤一何润，秀色若可餐).
story.zh: 陆机：“鲜肤一何润，秀色若可餐。”

usage.zh: 形容美貌或景色，有时带戏谑。

meaning.en: To ride with loose reins, letting the horse take its course; to stroll or think at will.
meaning.zh: 骑着马，放松缰绳，任马前行；比喻随意漫步或随意发挥。

examples.zh: 他在草原上信马由缰，心情舒畅。
examples.en: He rode with loose reins across the grassland, feeling easy.

examples.zh: 饭后我信马由缰地走了一圈。
examples.en: After dinner I wandered aimlessly for a stroll.

examples.zh: 写作时思绪信马由缰，难免跑题。
examples.en: When writing, thoughts roaming free may drift off topic.

natural: heart pierced by a thousand arrows

meaning.en: Agonising heartbreak or grief; also used as a curse.
meaning.zh: 像万支箭射穿心脏一样，形容极度痛苦；也用作咒骂的话。

equivalents: heart pierced by a thousand arrows

examples.zh: 听到噩耗，她如同万箭穿心。
examples.en: On hearing the terrible news, she felt as if her heart were pierced by countless arrows.

examples.zh: 看着孩子受苦，母亲万箭穿心。
examples.en: Watching her child suffer, the mother was in agony.

examples.zh: 他那一句话，让我万箭穿心。
examples.en: That one remark cut me to the heart.

meaning.en: A noble, upright spirit that lives on forever.
meaning.zh: 正大刚直的精神永远存在。

examples.zh: 烈士虽已牺牲，但浩气长存。
examples.en: The martyrs have fallen, but their noble spirit lives on.

examples.zh: 文天祥浩气长存，千古传颂。
examples.en: Wen Tianxiang's noble spirit lives on, praised through the ages.

examples.zh: 英雄精神浩气长存。
examples.en: The heroic spirit endures.

meaning.en: Exquisite and unrivalled.
meaning.zh: 精巧美妙到了无与伦比的程度。

examples.zh: 这件玉雕工艺精妙绝伦。
examples.en: The craftsmanship of this jade carving is exquisite beyond compare.

examples.zh: 他的演奏精妙绝伦，赢得满堂喝彩。
examples.en: His playing was superb and won a standing ovation.

examples.zh: 这篇文章构思精妙绝伦。
examples.en: The conception of this essay is exquisite.

natural: winners are kings, losers are bandits

meaning.en: The winner is hailed as a king and the loser branded a bandit.
meaning.zh: 成功了就是王侯，失败了就是贼寇，指以成败论英雄。

equivalents: history is written by the victors

examples.zh: 历史上成王败寇的例子比比皆是。
examples.en: History is full of cases where winners are kings and losers outlaws.

examples.zh: 商场上成王败寇，没有人同情失败者。
examples.en: In business it's winner takes all and nobody pities losers.

examples.zh: 他不接受成王败寇的评判标准。
examples.en: He refuses to judge people by success alone.

meaning.en: To bully someone excessively.
meaning.zh: 欺负人过分了。

examples.zh: 你们这样做，实在欺人太甚！
examples.en: What you've done goes too far!

examples.zh: 他一再羞辱我，简直欺人太甚。
examples.en: He has humiliated me again and again; it's too much.

examples.zh: 对方欺人太甚，我们不能再忍了。
examples.en: They have gone too far and we can no longer put up with it.

meaning.en: To leave no leeway or margin for retreat or compromise.
meaning.zh: 说话做事不留回旋的空间。

examples.zh: 说话别不留余地，以后还要相处。
examples.en: Don't leave yourself no room; you'll have to get on later.

examples.zh: 他做事不留余地，得罪了不少人。
examples.en: He leaves no margin in dealings and has offended many.

examples.zh: 谈判时双方都不留余地。
examples.en: Neither side left any room in the negotiations.

meaning.en: Being lenient to wrongdoers only encourages evil.
meaning.zh: 对坏人坏事一味宽容迁就，反而助长了坏人。

equivalents: spare the rod and spoil the criminal

examples.zh: 对违规行为不能姑息养奸。
examples.en: Violations must not be tolerated, or they will breed.

examples.zh: 执法不严就是姑息养奸。
examples.en: Lax enforcement just coddles wrongdoers.

examples.zh: 学校对欺凌姑息养奸，后果严重。
examples.en: If schools indulge bullying, the consequences are grave.

antonyms: 诸葛亮挥泪斩马谡——忍痛割爱

meaning.en: To instruct someone earnestly, as if pulling their ear while speaking to their face.
meaning.zh: 恳切地教导，好像拉着耳朵、当面嘱咐。

examples.zh: 老师对学生耳提面命，不厌其烦。
examples.en: The teacher instructs the students tirelessly and in person.

examples.zh: 父亲耳提面命，要他诚实做人。
examples.en: His father drilled into him the need to be honest.

examples.zh: 虽然师长耳提面命，他还是犯了错。
examples.en: Despite his elders' repeated admonitions, he still erred.

story.en: Book of Songs, 'Yi': 'Not only do I instruct you face to face, I take you by the ear' (匪面命之，言提其耳).

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC
